## Example

::demo[form-field-example]

The example above is this file, rendered live:

:::code form-field-example.ts

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component } from '@angular/core';
import { FormControl, FormGroup, ReactiveFormsModule, Validators } from '@angular/forms';
import {
  VoltError,
  VoltFormField,
  VoltHint,
  VoltInput,
  VoltLabel,
  VoltNativeButton,
} from '@voltui/components';

/**
 * Errors render once a field is touched (left, or the form submitted), so the alert is announced
 * then and not on every keystroke.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-form-field-example',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [
    ReactiveFormsModule,
    VoltFormField,
    VoltLabel,
    VoltHint,
    VoltError,
    VoltInput,
    VoltNativeButton,
  ],
  template: `
    <form class="mx-auto max-w-sm space-y-4" [formGroup]="login" (ngSubmit)="submit()" novalidate>
      <volt-form-field>
        <volt-label>Work email</volt-label>
        <volt-input formControlName="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required />
        <volt-hint>We only use it for account updates.</volt-hint>
        @if (login.controls.email.touched && login.controls.email.invalid) {
          <volt-error>Enter a valid email address.</volt-error>
        }
      </volt-form-field>

      <volt-form-field>
        <volt-label>Password</volt-label>
        <volt-input
          formControlName="password"
          type="password"
          autocomplete="current-password"
          required
        />
        <volt-hint>At least 8 characters.</volt-hint>
        @if (login.controls.password.touched && login.controls.password.invalid) {
          <volt-error>Use at least 8 characters.</volt-error>
        }
      </volt-form-field>

      <button voltButton type="submit" class="w-full">Sign in</button>
    </form>
  `,
})
export class FormFieldExample {
  readonly login = new FormGroup({
    email: new FormControl('', {
      nonNullable: true,
      validators: [Validators.required, Validators.email],
    }),
    password: new FormControl('', {
      nonNullable: true,
      validators: [Validators.required, Validators.minLength(8)],
    }),
  });

  submit(): void {
    // Shows every error at once; a real form would send the value when it is valid.
    this.login.markAllAsTouched();
  }
}
```

## Forms and accessibility

- Inside `<volt-form-field>`, `<volt-label>` labels the control through `aria-labelledby`, and clicking it focuses the control. No ids are needed; outside a form field, use `<volt-label htmlFor>`.
- `<volt-hint>` is always part of the control's description (`aria-describedby`).
- `<volt-error>` joins the description while it is rendered and the control's validators fail, and leaves it when it is removed: no reference to a removed message is left behind.
- `aria-invalid="true"` is set on the control (not on a wrapper) once it is invalid and touched, so the error is not conveyed by color alone.
- **Error announcement:** `<volt-error>` is an alert, announced when it is inserted. Render it once the field has been left or the form submitted (`@if (control.touched && control.invalid)`), as in the example, rather than on every keystroke. For validation that should wait until the reader leaves the field, use Angular's `updateOn: 'blur'`.
- One control per form field. Works with `volt-input`, `volt-textarea`, `volt-select` and native controls with `ngpInput`.

## Installation

Copy the source into your project:

```bash
npx @voltui/cli add form-field
```

Or import it from the package:

```bash
npm install @voltui/components
```

Copy this code to your project. The component uses `ng-primitives/form-field`.

:::code form-field.ts

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, computed, input } from '@angular/core';
import { NgpFormField } from 'ng-primitives/form-field';
import { cn } from '../../utils';

@Component({
  selector: 'volt-form-field',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  hostDirectives: [NgpFormField],
  host: {
    '[class]': 'classes()',
  },
  template: `<ng-content />`,
})
export class VoltFormField {
  readonly class = input<string>('');

  protected readonly classes = computed(() => cn('space-y-stack w-full block', this.class()));
}
```

:::code form-field-label.ts

```ts
import {
  booleanAttribute,
  ChangeDetectionStrategy,
  Component,
  computed,
  input,
} from '@angular/core';
import { NgTemplateOutlet } from '@angular/common';
import { injectFormFieldState, NgpLabel } from 'ng-primitives/form-field';
import { forwardClassFromHost } from '../../host-forwarding';
import { cn } from '../../utils';

/**
 * Renders a native `<label>`. Inside `<volt-form-field>` it is wired to the field's control
 * automatically; elsewhere pass `htmlFor`. `class` is applied to the `<label>`.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'volt-label',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [NgpLabel, NgTemplateOutlet],
  template: `
    <!--
      NgpLabel owns the label inside a form field (id, for, aria-labelledby on the control).
      Outside one it has no control to point at: it would drop the for attribute and cancel the
      native click, so a plain label with htmlFor is rendered instead.
    -->
    @if (formField()) {
      <!-- eslint-disable-next-line @angular-eslint/template/label-has-associated-control -->
      <label ngpLabel [class]="classes()">
        <ng-container [ngTemplateOutlet]="content" />
      </label>
    } @else {
      <label [class]="classes()" [attr.for]="htmlFor() || null">
        <ng-container [ngTemplateOutlet]="content" />
      </label>
    }
    <ng-template #content><ng-content /></ng-template>
  `,
})
export class VoltLabel {
  protected readonly formField = injectFormFieldState({ optional: true });

  readonly error = input<boolean, unknown>(false, { transform: booleanAttribute });
  readonly htmlFor = input<string>('');
  readonly class = input<string>('');

  protected readonly classes = computed(() =>
    cn(
      'text-sm font-medium text-foreground leading-none peer-disabled:cursor-not-allowed peer-disabled:opacity-70',
      this.error() && 'text-error',
      this.class()
    )
  );

  constructor() {
    forwardClassFromHost();
  }
}
```

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, computed, input } from '@angular/core';
import { NgpDescription } from 'ng-primitives/form-field';
import { forwardClassFromHost } from '../../host-forwarding';
import { cn } from '../../utils';

/** Field description, referenced by the control's `aria-describedby`. `class` styles the text. */
@Component({
  selector: 'volt-hint',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [NgpDescription],
  template: `
    <span ngpDescription [class]="classes()">
      <ng-content />
    </span>
  `,
})
export class VoltHint {
  readonly class = input<string>('');

  protected readonly classes = computed(() => cn('text-sm text-muted-foreground', this.class()));

  constructor() {
    forwardClassFromHost();
  }
}

:::code form-field-error.ts

```ts
import {
  ChangeDetectionStrategy,
  Component,
  computed,
  DestroyRef,
  inject,
  input,
  viewChild,
} from '@angular/core';
import { injectFormFieldState, NgpError } from 'ng-primitives/form-field';
import { forwardClassFromHost } from '../../host-forwarding';
import { cn } from '../../utils';

/**
 * Validation message. It is an alert, so a screen reader announces it when it is *inserted*: render it
 * once the field has been left or the form submitted (`@if (control.touched && control.invalid)`),
 * not on every keystroke. While it is rendered and its validator fails, the field's control lists it
 * in `aria-describedby`. `class` styles the text.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'volt-error',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  imports: [NgpError],
  template: `
    <span ngpError role="alert" aria-live="assertive" [class]="classes()">
      <ng-content />
    </span>
  `,
})
export class VoltError {
  readonly class = input<string>('');

  protected readonly classes = computed(() => cn('text-error text-sm font-medium', this.class()));

  private readonly formField = injectFormFieldState({ optional: true });
  private readonly error = viewChild.required(NgpError);

  constructor() {
    forwardClassFromHost();
    // ng-primitives unregisters an error on destroy only if it is still failing. An error removed
    // because the value became valid is destroyed in the same pass that clears the failure, so its
    // id stayed in the control's aria-describedby, pointing at an element that no longer exists.
    inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy(() => this.formField()?.removeDescription(this.error().id()));
  }
}
```
